intent: run command: validate the fetched manifest against the live JVM and start java with the archive flag, or plain
RunPlanner, run command and exec wrapper

title: run decides in Java and prints the command; a shell wrapper execs it; --spawn is the fallback
why: Java cannot replace its own process, so a Java-only wrapper keeps a second JVM resident (40-60 MB) and must forward signals. Printing the command lets sh exec it so the JVM is PID 1; failure of run falls back to the original command.
alternative: Resident Java supervisor only — rejected: memory cost and signal handling in the pod's main process

title: require build-time extraction and compare JAR modification times to the second; start plain on any difference
why: The JVM silently ignores an archive when JAR size or modification time differ, so run checks the times itself, logs why, and avoids the flag. Trainer and app must run the same extracted files.
alternative: Extract at startup and restore times — rejected: startup cost and fragile path/time restoration

title: RunPlanner never throws and never changes the command except to insert one flag after java
why: Every validation failure becomes a note and the original command; unsupported launches (-cp, main class, non-java) are left alone.
alternative: Fail on unsupported launches — rejected: would stop an application over an optimisation

name: RunPlanner
role: Validates fetched flags, manifest and archive against the live java launch and returns the command to execute
conditions: Only java ... -jar launches; archive flag inserted at index 1; command with its own archive flag is untouched

name: mnemo-warmup-exec
role: POSIX entrypoint: evals run --print then execs; execs the original command if run is absent or fails
conditions: Needs /bin/sh; run logs go to stderr, only the command to stdout

name: run command
role: --print for the wrapper, default/--spawn child process with SIGTERM forwarding; parse errors fall back to the original command after --

subject: exec and PID 1
why: A Java process cannot exec; letting sh exec the printed command keeps the JVM as PID 1 so Kubernetes SIGTERM reaches it

subject: Modification time precision
why: Compared to whole seconds because the JVM does; filesystems with finer timestamps would otherwise report false differences

title: hash the archive in run and record the training directory in the manifest
why: A size check accepts same-length corruption, and the JVM records JAR paths, so identical files in another directory are ignored. run hashes the archive against the manifest and compares launchDir, which is outside the fingerprint because paths and times can legitimately differ between trainer and replica.
alternative: Put the directory in the fingerprint — rejected: fetch would then miss instead of letting run explain the mismatch

title: --spawn waits for the child up to a bounded timeout on SIGTERM, then kills it
why: As PID 1, exiting right after destroy() makes the runtime kill the child before its shutdown hooks finish. Waiting (default 25 s, under the 30 s default grace period) then SIGKILL keeps shutdown clean and bounded.
alternative: Fire and forget destroy() — rejected: child loses its grace period

title: bound the whole JDK probe including output reading
why: The probe read the stream to EOF before its timed wait, so a hung launcher or agent holding the pipe blocked startup forever. Reading on a daemon thread with a deadline, then killing the process, keeps fallback reachable.
alternative: Keep the wait after readAllBytes — rejected: the timeout is never reached

subject: Reading a process's output blocks past waitFor
why: readAllBytes waits for EOF, which a left-behind child can hold open, so the timeout must wrap the read

subject: manifest launchDir
why: Optional in the JSON for older manifests; without it run cannot verify the training location and starts plain

subject: PID 1 and SIGTERM
why: When the spawning JVM is PID 1 it must outlive its child's shutdown, or the container runtime kills the child immediately
